name: Trestolone (MENT)
summary: Trestolone (MENT): an experimental potent androgen developed for male contraception and replacement, now floated on looksmax.org as a topical 'facial remodeling' idea with no supporting data.
lead: Trestolone, known in research as MENT, is a synthetic 19-nortestosterone-type androgen with a methyl group at the 7-alpha position. According to Grokipedia, an AI-generated encyclopedia, it was developed in the 1960s and later studied by the Population Council as a candidate for male hormonal contraception and androgen replacement; it has not been approved for medical use.
claims: Topical androgens like DHT, tren and MENT bind locally in the jawline and could remodel the face.
Androgens' effect on bone preservation implies bone growth.
MENT is a far more potent anabolic than testosterone.

name: Dimethandrolone undecanoate
summary: An experimental oral androgen-progestin built as a male contraceptive pill; no human data on muscle or looks.
lead: Dimethandrolone undecanoate (DMAU) is an experimental, orally active synthetic androgen with progestational activity. It is an ester prodrug: enzymes in the body cleave off the undecanoate group to release the active compound, dimethandrolone (7alpha,11beta-dimethyl-19-nortestosterone), a 19-nortestosterone derivative . It has been developed mainly as a candidate male hormonal contraceptive and, secondarily, as a possible androgen replacement therapy .
claims: DMAU could work as a future oral anabolic steroid
It is a promising male pill because it works at the hormone level
Fertility recovers fully after hormonal contraception trials

name: Methasterone
summary: An oral designer steroid once sold as the supplement Superdrol; users report fast muscle gain, case reports document liver and kidney injury, and no human trial exists.
lead: Methasterone (2alpha,17alpha-dimethyl-5alpha-androstan-17beta-ol-3-one, also called methyldrostanolone) is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from dihydrotestosterone. It was never approved as a medicine. In the 2000s it was sold in the United States under the brand name Superdrol as an over-the-counter bodybuilding supplement and was described by sellers as a prohormone, although forum users and laboratory studies have treated it as an active steroid itself .
claims: Superdrol builds lean muscle quickly with little water retention
It is among the most liver-toxic oral steroids
Non-aromatizing steroids like Superdrol and Winstrol can add height to teenagers
Post-cycle therapy and cholesterol support make it manageable

name: Androstenedione
summary: A weak natural androgen once sold as the 90s baseball-era testosterone-booster supplement; trials found no strength or muscle gains at ordinary doses.
lead: Androstenedione (androst-4-ene-3,17-dione, often called "andro" or A4) is an endogenous steroid hormone made in the adrenal glands and gonads. It is a weak androgen and an intermediate in the body's synthesis of testosterone and of estrone, and it can be converted in either direction between itself and testosterone . Its level in blood is used as a marker in conditions such as polycystic ovary syndrome and congenital adrenal hyperplasia .
claims: Oral androstenedione converts to testosterone and builds muscle
It is a weak androgen with mostly estrogenic downsides
Banned prohormones were replaced by relabelled analogues such as 1-andro

name: DHEA
summary: A natural adrenal hormone sold as an over-the-counter anti-aging and testosterone-support pill; solid for vaginal atrophy, thin for muscle or looks.
lead: Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA, also called androstenolone or prasterone) is an endogenous steroid precursor and one of the most abundant circulating steroids in humans. It is made mainly by the adrenal glands, with smaller amounts from the gonads and brain, and serves as an intermediate in the synthesis of androgens and estrogens; it also has weak direct hormonal and neurosteroid effects . Its sulfate ester, DHEA-S, is a stable marker of adrenal androgen activity .
claims: DHEA is a "fountain of youth" hormone that improves skin and should be kept high
DHEA can make you grow taller
Supplementing DHEA raises testosterone
Low DHEA-S can be fixed by supplementing

name: Dihydrotestosterone (DHT)
summary: The potent androgen behind puberty and balding; DHT gel is a forum favourite for face and penis claims with no trials in healthy people.
lead: Dihydrotestosterone (DHT, 5alpha-dihydrotestosterone, androstanolone) is an endogenous androgen made from testosterone by the enzyme 5alpha-reductase, mainly in tissues such as the prostate, skin and hair follicles. It binds the androgen receptor more strongly than testosterone and cannot be converted to estrogen by aromatase . It drives development of the male external genitalia in the fetus and, at puberty, facial and body hair, and it is implicated in male-pattern hair loss and prostate enlargement .
claims: DHT gel during puberty enhances facial bone masculinity
DHT gel grows the penis
DHT gel suppresses natural testosterone
DHT gel is useless for penile growth

name: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG)
summary: The pregnancy hormone that fertility clinics and TRT doctors use to keep testes working; forum claims for face, height and penis growth are untested.
lead: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) is a glycoprotein hormone made by the placenta after implantation, consisting of an alpha subunit shared with other gonadotropins and a hormone-specific beta subunit. It sustains the corpus luteum and progesterone production in early pregnancy and is the basis of pregnancy tests . Because it acts on the luteinizing hormone receptor, it is used as a prescription injectable to trigger ovulation in fertility treatment and to stimulate the testes in some men with low testosterone .
claims: hCG prevents testicular atrophy and preserves fertility on testosterone
hCG is needed on a low-dose first cycle
hCG improves facial growth alongside growth hormone
hCG, with or without DHT gel, can increase penis size

name: Andarine (S-4)
summary: An unapproved SARM from the early 2000s, known in forums for cutting use and for turning vision yellow-green; only animal data exist.
lead: Andarine, also known as S-4 and GTx-007, is an investigational, non-steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) of the aryl-propionamide class, structurally derived from the antiandrogen bicalutamide. It was developed in the early 2000s by researchers at the University of Tennessee and GTx, Inc., with the aim of producing the muscle and bone effects of androgens with fewer effects on tissues such as the prostate .
claims: S-4 causes yellow or green tinted vision and night blindness
S-4 helps with cutting while preserving muscle
S-4 spares hair and avoids steroid-type side effects
SARMs are safer than steroids

name: Cardarine (GW501516)
summary: A discontinued metabolic drug sold as a fat-loss and endurance aid; some lipid benefits in small trials, but rodent cancer findings ended its development.
lead: Cardarine, also known as GW501516, GW-1516 and Endurobol, is an experimental drug that selectively activates the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor delta (PPAR-delta). It was developed by Ligand Pharmaceuticals and GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) as a possible treatment for dyslipidemia and metabolic disease, and GSK stopped development in 2007 . It was later found to cause cancer in several organs in rodents at high doses, according to Wikipedia .
claims: Cardarine helps you get lean quickly
It is a milder option than clenbuterol
It causes cancer
It improves endurance

name: SR9009 (Stenabolic)
summary: A REV-ERB clock-receptor agonist sold as Stenabolic for endurance and cutting; mouse data only, nothing in humans, and a liver-injury case report.
lead: SR9009, sold under the name Stenabolic, is a synthetic small molecule that activates REV-ERB, a pair of nuclear receptors (REV-ERBα and REV-ERBβ) that help run the body's circadian clock and regulate metabolism and inflammation. It was developed as a laboratory tool compound and has been studied in cells and animals; it is not an approved medicine anywhere.
claims: Stenabolic boosts endurance and helps with cutting body fat
Stenabolic is a SARM
It can be stacked with Cardarine and other SARMs
Stenabolic is gentle enough to run during or after a steroid cycle

name: CJC-1295 with DAC
summary: A long-acting GHRH analogue (drug affinity complex) talked about for growth hormone stacks; unapproved and with no appearance trials behind it.
lead: CJC-1295 with DAC is a synthetic analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) that carries a drug affinity complex (DAC), a chemical attachment intended to bind blood proteins and prolong its action compared with shorter-acting GHRH analogues. It was developed by the Canadian company ConjuChem Biotechnologies and has not been approved as a medicine.
claims: Using several GHRH analogues together gives a better result than one
The version without DAC combined with ipamorelin is preferable to the DAC version

name: Modified GRF (1-29)
summary: A short-acting GHRH analogue (CJC-1295 no DAC) paired with GHRPs in forum stacks; no human trials for appearance.
lead: Modified GRF (1-29), also called Mod GRF, tetrasubstituted GRF (1-29) and CJC-1295 without DAC, is a synthetic 29-amino-acid analogue of the active fragment of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH). Four amino acid substitutions are described as making it more resistant to enzymatic breakdown than the natural sequence.  It has not been approved as a medicine.
claims: Pairing a GHRP with Mod GRF gives synergistic growth hormone release
It improves sleep and recovery
It is the best available GHRH analogue
What is sold online is what the label says

name: GHRP-2 (Pralmorelin)
summary: A potent ghrelin-receptor GH-releasing peptide: a real diagnostic in Japan, but nothing shows it builds muscle in healthy users.
lead: GHRP-2 (pralmorelin) is a synthetic hexapeptide that stimulates growth hormone (GH) release by acting on the ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor. It belongs to the family of growth hormone-releasing peptides developed from work led by Cyril Bowers at Tulane University and by Polygen in Germany.
claims: GHRP-2 raises GH, helping muscle growth and recovery
GHRP-2 can increase height
It improves sleep
GHRP-2 is preferable to GHRP-6 because it causes less hunger

name: Hexarelin (Examorelin)
summary: A potent GH-releasing peptide studied in 1990s endocrine trials; forum favourite, no evidence for looks, with desensitization questions.
lead: Hexarelin (also called examorelin) is a synthetic hexapeptide growth hormone-releasing peptide (GHRP) that stimulates growth hormone (GH) release by activating the growth hormone secretagogue receptor, the receptor for the gut hormone ghrelin.  Reviews describe it as more chemically stable and more potent than ghrelin itself.
claims: Hexarelin is the most potent GH peptide
GHRP plus GHRH gives synergistic GH release
Hexarelin builds muscle without water retention

name: Bimagrumab
summary: An investigational antibody that blocks muscle brakes; trials show fat loss and muscle preservation, but it is not available outside studies.
lead: Bimagrumab (BYM338, LY3985863) is an investigational fully human monoclonal antibody that blocks activin type II receptors (ActRIIA and ActRIIB), the receptors through which myostatin, activins and related signals restrain muscle growth.  It was developed by Novartis, and Eli Lilly acquired rights to it through its purchase of Versanis Bio in 2023, according to an AI-generated encyclopedia summary.

name: Survodutide
summary: A glucagon/GLP-1 dual agonist in phase 3; real weight-loss trials in obesity and liver disease, not yet approved.
lead: Survodutide (BI 456906) is an investigational once-weekly injectable peptide that activates both the glucagon receptor and the GLP-1 receptor. It is being developed by Boehringer Ingelheim for obesity, type 2 diabetes and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), and has not been approved as a medicine at the time of writing.

name: VK2735
summary: A GLP-1/GIP dual agonist in phase 3; phase 2 showed about 9 to 15% weight loss in 13 weeks, but it is still investigational.
lead: VK2735 is an investigational dual agonist of the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) receptors, developed by Viking Therapeutics for weight management. It is being tested as a weekly subcutaneous injection and as a daily oral formulation, and is not approved as a medicine.

name: CagriSema
summary: Not-yet-approved weekly semaglutide plus cagrilintide shot that cut weight about 20% in phase 3 trials.
lead: CagriSema is an investigational once-weekly injectable combination of cagrilintide, an amylin receptor agonist, and semaglutide, a GLP-1 receptor agonist, developed by Novo Nordisk for weight management . It is intended for adults with overweight or obesity, with or without type 2 diabetes, and is not an appearance product in itself; any effect on looks comes through fat loss.
claims: CagriSema "kicks ass" for fat loss alongside retatrutide

name: Exenatide
summary: Original Gila-monster-derived GLP-1 shot for type 2 diabetes with only modest weight loss, long since eclipsed by semaglutide.
lead: Exenatide is a synthetic peptide that activates the GLP-1 receptor and is approved in the United States as an adjunct to diet and exercise for adults with type 2 diabetes. It is based on exendin-4, a hormone first identified in the saliva of the Gila monster, and was first marketed as Byetta, a twice-daily injection, in 2005 . An extended-release once-weekly form, Bydureon, followed .
claims: Exenatide-type GLP-1 drugs could help with fat loss
Exenatide may increase beta-cell number or function

name: Tesofensine
summary: Never-approved triple reuptake inhibitor that cut weight 4.5% to 10.6% beyond placebo in a 24-week trial, with heart-rate and blood-pressure rises.
lead: Tesofensine (development code NS2330) is an investigational oral drug that blocks the reuptake of dopamine, noradrenaline and serotonin. It was developed by the Danish company NeuroSearch, first for Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease, and then pursued as an obesity treatment after weight loss was observed in those trials .
claims: Tesofensine produces strong appetite suppression and fat loss
It is a safe alternative to approved weight-loss drugs

name: Orlistat
summary: OTC and Rx fat-absorption blocker that adds a few kilos of weight loss over placebo at the price of oily stools.
lead: Orlistat is a gastrointestinal lipase inhibitor used with a reduced-calorie diet for weight loss in adults. It is sold by prescription as Xenical (120 mg capsules) and over the counter as Alli (60 mg capsules), and it works inside the gut rather than being absorbed into the bloodstream . Reviews describe it as one of five or so drugs available for long-term obesity treatment in the US, with weight loss smaller than that of newer injectable drugs .
claims: Orlistat blocks fat absorption so it helps cutting
Orlistat is ineffective for people already on a low-fat diet
Orlistat is a safe replacement for banned stimulants

name: Naltrexone/Bupropion (Contrave)
summary: Prescription pill pairing an opioid blocker with an antidepressant for appetite control; solid but modest weight loss next to GLP-1 drugs.
lead: Naltrexone/bupropion, sold as Contrave (Mysimba in some markets), is a fixed-dose oral combination of an opioid-receptor antagonist and an antidepressant and smoking-cessation drug, approved for chronic weight management in adults with obesity or overweight alongside diet and exercise . It is one of the centrally acting weight-loss drugs reviewed alongside phentermine-topiramate .

name: Phentermine
summary: Decades-old prescription stimulant appetite suppressant with short-term, modest weight loss and cardiovascular warnings.
lead: Phentermine is a sympathomimetic amine with an amphetamine-like profile, sold by prescription as an appetite suppressant and approved in the US as a short-term adjunct, usually described as a few weeks, to diet, exercise and behavior change in adults with obesity . Grokipedia dates its FDA approval to 1959 and lists brands including Adipex-P, Lomaira and Duromine .

name: Phentermine/Topiramate (Qsymia)
summary: Once-daily phentermine plus topiramate capsule with clear weight loss over placebo, though behind GLP-1 injections, and a pregnancy risk.
lead: Phentermine/topiramate extended-release (Qsymia) is a fixed-dose capsule combining phentermine, a sympathomimetic amine, with topiramate, an anticonvulsant, taken once daily to reduce appetite and increase satiety . It was approved by the US FDA in 2012 for chronic weight management and in July 2022 became the first approved for pediatric use of this combination, as noted in a review of that approval . The marketer cited in that review is VIVUS .

name: Clenbuterol
summary: Asthma-drug stimulant used as a gray-market cutting pill, with a documented record of heart problems.
lead: Clenbuterol is a long-acting beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist developed as a bronchodilator for asthma and airway obstruction. It is prescribed in some countries for respiratory disease and in veterinary medicine, mainly for horses, but it is not approved for human use in the United States . It is on prohibited-substance lists in sport, and a 1995 review described its popularity with athletes for purported anabolic effects and reduction of subcutaneous fat .
claims: Clen is a cheap way to get shredded
Clen is stronger than GW (cardarine) but has worse side effects
It increases vascularity
Clen plus DNP and other drugs produce dramatic transformations

name: 2,4-Dinitrophenol (DNP)
summary: A 1930s diet drug that melts fat by turning cells into heaters; the narrow gap between effective and lethal is why it is banned for human use.
lead: 2,4-Dinitrophenol (DNP) is a yellow crystalline industrial chemical that has been used in explosives, pesticides and dyes, and that was briefly sold as a weight-loss drug in the United States in the 1930s . It acts as a mitochondrial uncoupler: it makes cells release energy as heat rather than storing it as ATP, which raises metabolic rate .
claims: DNP is a "super effective cut" that produces about 8-10 lb of fat loss in three weeks.
The risks are manageable with hydration, avoiding summer heat and starting at lower doses.
Testosterone plus retatrutide and a structured diet outperforms DNP, so DNP is unnecessary.
DNP can be sourced online from supplement vendors or EU suppliers.

name: Ephedrine
summary: The stimulant in the classic ECA stack: modest fat loss in trials, but a pulse-and-pressure raiser that the FDA banned from supplements.
lead: Ephedrine is a sympathomimetic amine and central nervous system stimulant found naturally in plants of the genus Ephedra (ma huang) and also made synthetically . It acts on adrenergic receptors and triggers release of norepinephrine, producing raised blood pressure, heart rate and alertness . In current US medical practice it is a prescription injectable indicated for clinically important hypotension during anesthesia .
claims: The ECA stack kills appetite and gives energy for fasted cardio while preserving lean tissue.
ECA is a mild thermogenic, much weaker than clenbuterol, albuterol or DNP.
It is acceptable if you have no heart problems and track heart rate, and exercise should be low-intensity.
Ephedrine can be stacked with MK-677 to counter hunger while building muscle and height.

name: Sibutramine
summary: A withdrawn prescription appetite suppressant that worked modestly for weight loss but raised cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients.
lead: Sibutramine, sold as Meridia (US) and Reductil (elsewhere), is a serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor that was approved as an appetite suppressant for obesity and later withdrawn from major markets over cardiovascular safety concerns . Randomised trials found it produced modest weight loss beyond diet and exercise .
claims: Sibutramine is a strong appetite suppressant that can substitute for or complement an ECA stack.
Combining appetite suppressants and other agents improves fat loss.
Sibutramine remains safe to use outside medical supervision.

name: Ketoconazole
summary: Antifungal dandruff shampoo that hair-loss communities add to finasteride and minoxidil; small studies hint at benefit, large trials are missing.
lead: Ketoconazole is a synthetic imidazole antifungal. It is available as oral tablets for serious fungal infections and as topical creams, foams and shampoos (such as Nizoral) for skin and scalp conditions including dandruff, seborrheic dermatitis and pityriasis versicolor .
claims: Nizoral reduces shedding and may help male pattern baldness beyond treating dandruff.
Ketoconazole blocks conversion of testosterone to DHT.
Early shedding after starting ketoconazole is normal.
Frequent use can dry and irritate the scalp and skin.

name: Baricitinib
summary: A prescription JAK inhibitor approved for severe alopecia areata (autoimmune hair loss), not for ordinary pattern baldness, and carrying a boxed warning.
lead: Baricitinib (brand name Olumiant) is an oral Janus kinase (JAK) 1 and 2 inhibitor developed by Incyte and Eli Lilly and approved for rheumatoid arthritis, severe alopecia areata and hospitalised COVID-19 . For hair, it is relevant to alopecia areata, an autoimmune condition causing patchy or total hair loss, rather than to common male pattern baldness .
